update_usage: Usage: `/update <name>` or `/update <glob>` (e.g. `/update gluetun-*`). Updates only matching containers that have a pending update.
help_detail_update:
*/update* — Update containers by name or glob

`/update <name>` — check + update one container (if it has an update).
`/update <glob>` — update every matching container that has a pending update, e.g. `/update gluetun-*`.

📌 Runs a check first, then applies only matching containers with updates — same path as the Update-all button (group order, dependents cascade, health-check + rollback). Typing the pattern is the go-ahead, so no extra confirm. Use `/check <glob>` first to preview.
lifecycle_refused_protected: 🛡 `{name}` is protected from Stop. Remove the protection first (container detail page in the Web UI, or `/protect {name}`). Restart still works.
web_detail_protect_hint: Hide and refuse the Stop action for this container, so you can't accidentally take down something you depend on (e.g. the VPN/tunnel carrying your remote access). Restart and updates still work.
help_protect: /protect — Protect a container from being stopped
help_detail_protect:
*/protect* — Protect a container from Stop

`/protect` — list protected containers.
`/protect <name>` — toggle stop-protection for a container.

📌 A protected container has no Stop button (Telegram + Web UI) and Stop is refused — so you can't accidentally take down something you depend on, like the VPN/tunnel carrying your remote access. Restart and updates still work. Also settable on the container detail page in the Web UI.
protect_empty: No stop-protected containers. `/protect <name>` to add one.
protect_on: 🛡 `{name}` is now protected from Stop. Restart still works.
protect_off: `{name}` is no longer protected from Stop.

changelog_current:
📄 *You're on the latest — v{version}* ({date})
What this version brought:
cooldown_empty: No per-container update cooldowns set. `/cooldown <name> <seconds>` to add one.
cooldown_bad_value: ⚠️ Seconds must be a number (0–600). E.g. `/cooldown llama-server 20`.
cooldown_set: ✅ `{name}` update cooldown set to *{seconds}s* — Docksentry will pause that long after recreating it before the next container.
help_detail_cooldown:
*/cooldown* — Per-container update cooldown

`/cooldown` — list containers with a cooldown set.
`/cooldown <name> <seconds>` — after recreating this container in a batch update, Docksentry waits this long before recreating the next one (0–600s; 0 clears).
`/cooldown <name>` — show the current value.

📌 For heavy containers (GPU/large RAM) whose load peak would otherwise overlap the next recreate and exhaust memory. Opt-in, default 0. Also settable on the container detail page in the Web UI.
web_detail_cooldown_hint: After recreating this container in a batch update, wait this many seconds before the next one. For heavy GPU/RAM containers whose startup peak would otherwise overlap the next recreate and run out of memory. 0 = off.
selfupdate_retag: 🔁 *Re-joining the rolling line* — the image bits are identical, but I'll recreate so your container tracks `{new}` instead of `{old}` from now on. Bot will be briefly offline.
groups_none: No container groups configured yet. Create one in the Web UI → Groups.
groups_not_found: ⚠️ No group matching `{name}`. Try /groups to list them.
group_detail_rd_on: 🔁 restart-dependents: *on* — updating the head restarts the others
help_detail_groups:
*/groups* — Container Groups

`/groups` — list all groups with member count and the 👑 head.
`/groups <name>` — one group's members (🟢 running / ⚪ stopped), its restart-dependents setting, and — for a `restart_dependents` group — a button to restart the dependents now (waits for the head to be healthy first).

📌 Read-only except the restart button. Create / edit groups in the Web UI → Groups.

web_windows_days_hint: Leave all unchecked to allow every weekday.
web_major_pending_intro: These containers have a pending major-version bump. Major updates can break configs — confirm or skip.
web_settings_intro: Configure how Docksentry checks for, applies, and notifies about updates. Changes here override the corresponding environment variables and persist across restarts.
web_cron_help: 5-field cron expression (minute hour day month weekday). Default 0 18 * * * = daily at 18:00.
web_excluded_help: Comma-separated list of container names to skip during checks (e.g. 'plex,nextcloud'). Useful for containers you only want to update manually.
web_debug_help: Send detailed update-check logs to Telegram on every run. Useful for diagnosing why a container is or isn't being seen.
web_auto_selfupdate_help: When on, Docksentry pulls and applies its own image update on every scheduled cron tick. Off = self-update only on demand via /selfupdate or the maintenance button.
web_updates_tab_hint: Per-container auto-update flags, pin/unpin, and the major-confirm toggle live on the Status page — pick which containers get treated which way there.
web_topic_id_help: Optional. Set this to send Telegram messages to a specific topic/thread inside a forum-style group, instead of the general topic.
web_discord_help: Optional. Set to a Discord channel webhook URL to mirror updates as rich embeds in Discord. Find it under: Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
web_webhook_help: Optional. Generic JSON POST endpoint — works with Ntfy, Gotify, Home Assistant, n8n, etc. Receives all events as JSON payloads.
web_maintenance_intro: Manual one-shot actions. Each runs in the background and reports the result via the configured notification channels.
web_maintenance_explain: Image Cleanup removes unused Docker images older than {grace}h. With Backup local-only enabled, locally-built images are saved as tarballs in {dir} and kept for {days} days. Self-Update pulls the latest Docksentry image and recreates this container.

web_setup_cron_help: Format: minute hour day month weekday. Example: 0 18 * * * = daily at 18:00.

maintenance_enabled_forever: 🛠 Maintenance mode enabled — until manually disabled.

Use for VPN-sidecar / shared-network-namespace setups where dependents lose connectivity when the namespace owner restarts.

changelog_container_source:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

Docksentry doesn't fetch and parse arbitrary container changelogs — projects use too many different formats (Keep-a-Changelog, GitHub Releases, HISTORY.md, none at all) for a reliable summary. Instead, here's the upstream source:

🔗 {url}

Releases are typically at `/releases` and changelog files at `/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md`.
changelog_container_url_only:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

This image only sets the `image.url` label (product page, not source repo), so I can't link you directly at the changelog. Try:

🔗 {url}

Look for a 'Changelog', 'Release notes', or 'What's new' section.
changelog_container_none:
📄 *Changelog for* `{name}`

No source label and the image reference doesn't map to a known registry. Check the image's documentation or `docker inspect {name}` for hints.
web_link_intro: このコンテナ用の任意の URL — ソースリポジトリ、リリースページ、または変更履歴。更新通知ではコンテナ名にリンクとして付き、Web UI ではコンテナの横に 🔗 として表示されます。OCI ラベルからの自動検出より優先されます。空にすると自動検出に戻ります。compose ファイルの docksentry.link ラベルはこの項目より優先されます。
help_setlink: /setlink <name> <url> — Set the changelog / repo link shown in /changelog and update notifications. Omit URL to clear.
setlink_usage: Usage: `/setlink container_name https://github.com/...` — or `/setlink container_name` to clear.
setlink_cleared: 🔗 `{name}` link cleared — OCI labels will be used again.
help_per_command_hint: 💬 *Per-command help:* `/help <command>` shows parameters, examples and side effects for one command, e.g. `/help cleanup`.
help_detail_status:
*/status* — Container overview

`/status` — list of all containers (running + stopped) with health icons, uptime and image.
`/status <name>` — full detail for one container: state, health, ports, volumes, restart policy, plus inline action buttons (Update / Restart / Stop).

📌 Partial name matches work: `/status jelly` resolves to `jellyfin` if unambiguous.
help_detail_check:
*/check* — Trigger an update check now

Forces an immediate scan instead of waiting for the next `CRON_SCHEDULE` tick. Compares the local image digest of every running container against the registry. Pending updates land in a new "🔄 Updates Available" notification with one-tap buttons.

⚠️ Refuses while an update is already running (race-lock since v1.18.9).
help_detail_updates:
*/updates* — Show pending updates

Lists every container Docksentry has previously flagged as having an update available, with action buttons. Equivalent to re-displaying the last "Updates Available" notification without re-running the check.

📌 Empty when nothing is pending.
help_detail_cleanup:
*/cleanup* — Remove unused Docker images

Removes images older than `CLEANUP_GRACE_HOURS` (default 24h) that no running container references. Set `CLEANUP_BACKUP_LOCAL_ONLY=true` to back locally-built images up as tarballs first (in `/data/backups/`).

⚠️ Side effects: posts a notification, frees disk. Check before / after with `/status`.
help_detail_lifecycle:
*/start /stop /restart* — Single-container lifecycle

`/start <name>` — start a stopped container
`/stop <name>` — stop a running container (refuses on self for safety)
`/restart <name>` — stop + start in one shot

Partial name matches work. Stop refuses on the Docksentry container itself.
help_detail_maintenance:
*/maintenance* — Pause scheduled checks

`/maintenance <duration>` — silence auto-updates for the duration (e.g. `2h`, `30m`, `1d`, `forever`).
`/maintenance off` — re-enable immediately.
`/maintenance` (no arg) — show current state.

📌 Manual `/check` and `/update` still work during maintenance. Only the cron-driven auto-update is paused.
help_detail_history:
*/history* — Recent update history

Last 20 update events (success + failure) with date arrows, image size deltas and version arrows when the upstream image carries an `org.opencontainers.image.version` label. Includes self-updates of Docksentry itself since v1.17.6.
help_detail_pin:
*/pin /unpin* — Skip / re-enable updates for a container

`/pin <name>` — exclude from update checks (won't appear in `/updates`)
`/unpin <name>` — re-include
`/pin` (no arg) — list pinned

📌 Useful when you want to stay on a specific image version without env-var pinning.
help_detail_autoupdate:
*/autoupdate* — Toggle silent auto-update for a container

`/autoupdate <name>` — flip auto-update on / off for that container
`/autoupdate` (no arg) — list containers with auto-update enabled

📌 Auto-updated containers don't generate a "Updates Available" prompt — they run on the next cron tick with no button-tap needed. Use carefully: combine with `restart_dependents` Container Groups when a container has sidecars.
help_detail_setlink:
*/setlink* — コンテナのリポジトリ／変更履歴リンクを設定

`/setlink <名前> <url>` — リンクを保存（完全な `http://` または `https://` の URL が必要です。それ以外は拒否されます）
`/setlink <名前>`（url なし）— 削除してラベルによる検出に戻す

📌 コンテナラベル `docksentry.link` はこのコマンドより優先されます。compose ファイルに書けば、リンクはコンテナと一緒に移動します。
📌 このリンクは `/changelog` の出力、更新通知のリポジトリリンク、そして Web UI の 🔗 アイコンに使われます。上流イメージが OCI ラベル `org.opencontainers.image.source` を設定していない場合に便利です。
help_detail_audit:
*/audit* — Inspect-coverage audit for a container

`/audit <name>` — run the v1.19.0 audit logger against this container's `docker inspect` and report any HostConfig / Config fields that are non-default but NOT restored on recreate.

📌 If the output is empty, you're safe — every important field is preserved. If anything shows up, please file an issue with the lines so we can extend coverage.
help_detail_selfupdate:
*/selfupdate* — Update Docksentry itself

`/selfupdate` — pull `:latest` and recreate (helper-container swap)
`/selfupdate <X.Y.Z>` — pin to a specific version (e.g. `/selfupdate 1.19.0`)
`/selfupdate previous` — roll back to the last released version older than the running one

📌 Different code path than container updates — `selfupdate` uses a helper container to swap PID 1.
help_detail_changelog:
*/changelog* — What's new

`/changelog` — list Docksentry releases newer than the running version, with links
`/changelog <name>` — show the repo / changelog link for one container

📌 We don't try to fetch and parse arbitrary container changelogs (formats vary too much) — for containers we point you at the upstream source repo.
help_detail_debug:
*/debug* — Toggle debug logging

`/debug` — flip debug on / off. When on, internal events (cron ticks, network attach, audit-mode warnings, container resolve hits) appear in `docker logs docksentry`.

📌 No impact on Telegram chat output — only on host-side logs.
help_detail_logs:
*/logs* — Show recent container logs

`/logs <name>` — last 30 log lines from the container, formatted as a code block.

📌 Useful right after an update report: `❌ jellyfin: …rolled back` → then `/logs jellyfin` to see what crashed.
help_detail_lang:
*/lang* — Switch the bot language

`/lang en` or `/lang de` — change to English or German. Other 14 languages fall back to English strings (translation contributions welcome).
`/lang` (no arg) — show current language.
help_detail_settings:
*/settings* — Current configuration

Shows the active schedule, language, auto-selfupdate flag, healthcheck max-starting wait, debug state and other env-driven settings. Read-only via Telegram; the Web UI lets you edit most of these without restart.
help_detail_help:
*/help* — Command reference

`/help` — list of all commands with a one-line summary
`/help <command>` — detailed help for a specific command (synopsis, parameters, examples)

📌 The autocomplete picker (type `/` in this chat) is faster for discovery — try it.
audit_usage: Usage: `/audit container_name` — checks the container's inspect for fields we don't restore on recreate.
audit_clean: ✅ `{name}`: clean — every non-default HostConfig and Config field is restored on recreate.
audit_findings_header:
🔍 *Audit for* `{name}`:

The following fields are non-default in your inspect but NOT restored by `_build_run_args`. On recreate they'd be silently dropped.
audit_footer: 📬 Please [open an issue](https://github.com/amayer1983/docksentry/issues) with this list so we can extend coverage.
web_groups_page_intro: Manage VPN-sidecar / shared-namespace stacks here. The first container in a group is the *head* — when it's updated, dependents are restarted (if you enable `restart_dependents`). Drag rows to reorder.
web_groups_head_tt: The head container — when it's updated, the rest of the group reacts (restart, recreate, etc).
web_groups_stale_tt: This container no longer exists on the host. Edit the group to remove it.
web_groups_drag_tt: Drag to reorder. The first one is the head.
web_groups_no_members: No containers in this group yet.
web_groups_moved_intro: Container Groups now live on their own page with drag-and-drop reorder, edit-in-place, head-container visualisation, stale-member warnings, and auto-detect from Compose / Portainer stacks.
web_groups_autodetect_intro: Each card is a detected stack (containers grouped by `com.docker.compose.project` or `com.docker.stack.namespace`). Check the ones you want to import as Docksentry groups. Drag rows inside a card to set the head order before importing.
web_groups_autodetect_none: No Compose / Portainer / Swarm stacks detected on this host. Stacks need the standard project labels — manual `docker run` containers can't be auto-detected.
web_groups_autodetect_conflict: ⚠ Already in group `{group}` — will be moved on import.
web_groups_autodetect_skip_existing: Stack already imported (group exists with same name)
data_loss_alert:
⚠️ *No persisted settings found* — possible data loss.

Your Telegram config came from env vars, but `/data/settings.json` is missing. Container groups, pin / autoupdate / link / window state may have been lost too. Common causes: host reboot mid-write (fixed in v1.22.0 with atomic writes — won't happen again), volume mount missing at start, fresh `/data/` volume.

If you have a backup, restore via Web UI → Settings → Import. Otherwise re-configure and check the Web UI's Status page for any groups / pins you'd set up.
web_backup_intro: Export every persisted setting (groups, notes, links, pins, autoupdate flags, update windows, webhook URLs, etc.) into a single JSON file. Restore it later — useful before host migrations, or just as defense-in-depth against data loss.
web_backup_hint: Backups contain webhook URLs and bot tokens — treat the file like a password. The import path skips unknown keys, so forward-compatible if a future Docksentry adds new settings.
update_snapshot_stale_msg: ⚠️ That "Updates Available" notification is too old to act on (a newer check has replaced it, or the bot restarted). Run /check for a fresh list.
selfupdate_old_tag:
✅ The `:{current}` image tag is up to date — but that's a *fixed version*, and a newer release (`v{latest}`) exists. Your container won't move past `:{current}` on its own. To upgrade:
• `/selfupdate {latest}` (jump to the new version), or
• `/selfupdate latest` (rejoin the rolling latest line), or
• set `image: amayer1983/docksentry:latest` in your compose and `docker compose up -d`.
policy_held: ⏸ `{name}`: held back by update policy ({level} {old} → {new}). Run /update {name} to apply, or set docksentry.policy=all.
